mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Exclusive Consular Legalization/Cross-Strait Notarization Verification path (non-Hague; Taiwan is not a Hague Apostille Contracting Party for PRC purposes): (1) Taiwan notary public or district court certifies the certificate; (2) apply to the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) for verification; (3) SEF transmits the notarized copy to the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS); (4) present the notarized original to the designated mainland Notaries' Association for cross-strait verification; (5) a mainland notary office issues a certified Chinese-language translation; then use before SAMR, banks and tax authorities. ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before engagement, the compliance team must screen every proposed shareholder, director, supervisor, UBO, officer and authorized signatory against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU sanctions framework, the HKSAR sanctions notices, and the People's Bank of China risk, money-laundering and terrorist-financing lists. The protocol requires real-time politically exposed person (PEP) screening covering foreign political figures, senior PRC officials, state-owned enterprise executives, immediate family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence for any PEP, sanctions, adverse media or politically connected exposure; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification for all screening hits; suspicious transaction reporting to the China Financial Intelligence Monitoring Center; and retention of all screening records for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Registration System administered by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the Integrated Enterprise Registration Online Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every PRC company name must be in standardized Chinese characters; pinyin alone is not acceptable as the legal name. The statutory four-tier naming order is: administrative division, distinct trade name, industry or operating characteristics, and organizational form; for example, Shanghai AAA Webnovel Culture Co., Ltd. A WFOE may also record an English or foreign-language name for customs, banking and publishing identification, but the Chinese name governs. The foreign name must be a faithful transliteration or translation, must not contain unauthorized abbreviations, must not infringe prior trademarks, and must not be misleading as to the nature of the business.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Zhonghua / China / Chinese (prohibited unless specially approved by SAMR under central policy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five business days of an electronic name rejection notice, the applicant's designated agent must access the SAMR Enterprise Registration Online Service, locate the rejection decision, and file a written administrative review request under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the People's Republic of China with the next higher SAMR authority or the relevant local market regulation bureau. The appeal must state the legal basis, the cleared four-tier name structure, the absence of any listed prohibited token, evidence of prior trademark search, and a corrected proposed name; attach the rejection notice and identity authorization. The reviewing authority must decide within 15 working days; if rejected again, the applicant may institute an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a China WFOE operating a Serialized Digital Web Fiction and Interactive Reading App with Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payment rails, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally impermissible as the sole registered address. SAMR requires a registered address to be a fixed, tangible business site capable of receiving judicial, tax and regulatory correspondence, invoices and inspection officers. Municipal tax bureaus in most Tier-1 cities reject a virtual/mailbox address where the entity declares domestic revenue, issues digital VAT invoices, or maintains a merchant or app payment settlement flow. Commercial banks similarly reject a virtual office for corporate account opening, e-banking enrollment, contract signing and documentary verification unless the address sits within a recognized free-trade zone or government-supported cluster address scheme with a dedicated desk and lease continuity. Even where a legal 'park address' is permissible, the WFOE must demonstrate commercial substance through a valid lease, site photographs, utilities, local personnel, payroll, accounting books and a physical operational location for mainland user activities and payment merchant administration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist and quantified risk: estimated 65% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months. Risk triggers: (1) registered address appears on a shared or cluster registration list, increasing inspection likelihood by 40%; (2) no local employees or payroll records, increasing likelihood by 25%; (3) Apple/Google payment settlement routed through offshore or intermediate accounts, increasing likelihood by 20%; (4) inconsistency between tax declarations and registered industry, increasing likelihood by 25%. Inspection authorities include the municipal tax bureau, market regulation bureau, and public security agencies. Mitigation: post a compliant nameplate at the registered site, maintain the lease and utility records at the site, retain statutory books and vouchers, appoint a tax-attentive agent, and ensure at least one responsible person with authority is physically present in mainland China.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as most recently amended on 26 December 2018; applicable provisions include Article 6 (Registrability), Article 8 (Statutory Officers), Article 15 (Business Scope Limit), Article 101 (Required Articles of Incorporation), Article 128 (Supervisor and Corporate Governance), Article 156 (Paid-in Share Capital), Article 172 (Notice of Shareholder Meetings), Article 203 (Board Meeting Rules), Article 208 (Chairperson), Article 218 (Supervisor Powers), Article 387 (Application Filing and Formats), and Article 394 (Registration Fees); together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and the Regulations on Investment Registration of Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce — Company Registration Section, Taiwan (ROC); for foreign investment matters, the MOEA Investment Commission.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Registration under Article 387 of the Companies Act (Company Registration Application Form and Business Registration Form).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital; however, the entire registered capital must be fully subscribed and actually remitted to a licensed Taiwan bank before the registration application, evidenced by an inward remittance certificate. No blocked escrow account is required; the capital may be used for operating expenses after registration, but false capital or withdrawal before registration is prohibited under Article 9 of the Companies Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LTD. (TAIWAN) — ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF THE SOLE DIRECTOR AND SHAREHOLDER. WHEREAS, the company is a wholly foreign-owned enterprise limited liability company being formed under the Companies Act of Taiwan (Republic of China) with an intended business scope of serialized digital web fiction and interactive reading applications; WHEREAS, the articles of incorporation authorize an initial share capital of [amount] New Taiwan Dollars divided into [number] ordinary shares with par value of NT$10 each; WHEREAS, the formation stage requires confirmation of share subscription, adoption of a registered office, appointment of statutory officers, and authorization of banking arrangements. NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: FIRST: Share Capital Subscription and Payment. The board confirms that the issued share capital has been fully subscribed by the sole corporate shareholder and that payment in the full amount has been made to the company's foreign currency share capital collection account maintained at a licensed bank in Taiwan. The inward remittance certificate shall be retained and submitted to the Ministry of Economic Affairs as evidence of paid-in capital. The board ratifies the allotment of the subscribed shares to the shareholder. SECOND: Statutory Officers. The board appoints [Name] as Chairperson and Director; [Name] as Director; [Name] as Director; and [Name] as Supervisor (the 'statutory officers'), effective immediately. The Chairperson is authorized to act as the principal legal representative; the General Manager, [Name], is appointed as the highest executive officer; and [Name] is appointed as Company Secretary, responsible for filings, statutory books, and corporate records. THIRD: Banking Authorization. The board authorizes the General Manager and Company Secretary, jointly or either one together with the Chairperson, to open and manage corporate bank accounts, including New Taiwan dollar and foreign currency accounts, with any licensed bank in Taiwan, to execute signature cards, deposit and withdrawal slips, loan agreements, foreign exchange contracts, electronic banking mandates, and to use such accounts for subscription proceeds, Apple App Store In-App Purchase and Google Play Billing settlements, tax payments, salary disbursements, and operating expenses. FOURTH: Registered Office. The board adopts the premises at [registered address], Taipei, Taiwan, as the company's registered office for service of process, statutory records, and all official notices. The Company Secretary shall display a corporate nameplate, maintain statutory books, and notify the Company Registration Section if the office is relocated. FIFTH: Filings and Delegation. The board authorizes the Chairperson, General Manager, and Company Secretary, each acting jointly, to execute and submit the Application for Company Registration, Articles of Incorporation, foreign investment approval, Statement of Paid-in Capital, shareholder identity documents, director and supervisor consent forms, and any required certificate, to pay official fees, and to obtain the Company Registration Certificate and Business Registration Certificate. SIXTH: Effectiveness and Governing Law. This resolution is of full force and effect on the date of adoption and may be produced to any governmental authority, bank, or commercial counterparty. No further shareholder approval is required for the actions described unless mandatory under the Companies Act. This resolution is governed by the laws of Taiwan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Investment Commission — Online Foreign Investment Application System; MOEA Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Query System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: First, conduct a company name pre-search in the MOEA name reservation system to ensure the proposed English and Chinese names are not identical to reserved or registered names and are not prohibited for an information service company. Next, prepare and submit the foreign investment application electronically through the MOEA Investment Commission portal, selecting the business scope 'Serialized digital web fiction and interactive reading application,' specifying the country of origin of the foreign shareholder and the amount of external capital. Attach the foreign shareholder's corporate resolution approving incorporation, audited financial statements or a statement of capital availability, a notarized board resolution or power of attorney, and a formation chart for the ultimate beneficial owner. The Investment Commission reviews for prohibited or restricted business categories and national security concerns. If the commission issues a non-objection letter or approval, reserve the company name on the same portal. This approval and name reservation are valid for six months and may be renewed once before expiry.
required_dossiers: Completed foreign investment application form
Foreign corporate shareholder's board resolution authorizing the WFOE establishment
Audited financial statements or capital availability evidence of the foreign shareholder
Notarized power of attorney appointing Taiwan local representative
Proposed English and Chinese company names
Business scope description 'Serialized digital web fiction and interactive reading application'
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration and passport/corporate registration copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission queries by supplement letter, file an explanatory memo and amended application within the 14-day response window; if the name is rejected for similarity, re-query and submit a differentiated name with a legal explanation of distinctiveness. If approval is suspended for policy review, apply for a formal adjudication and, if necessary, revisit the capital structure to comply with any foreign investment restriction ratio.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Taiwanese banking institution (foreign exchange bank) and the Taiwan District Court Notary / licensed civil law notary public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving investment approval, open a temporary capital collection account (either foreign currency or New Taiwan dollar) with the chosen bank and remit the subscribed share capital from the foreign corporate shareholder's bank account, with the remittance purpose clearly marked as 'share capital subscription.' Obtain the bank's remittance receipt or electronic inward remittance certificate. The Taiwan local incorporator should execute the Articles of Incorporation, the Shareholders' Written Resolution consenting to incorporation, and the Statement of Paid-in Capital signed by the shareholder. These documents and the foreign shareholder's resolution should be notarized before the competent notary or authenticated through the Taiwan overseas mission in the shareholder's home jurisdiction. The articles must state the number and par value of shares, the business scope, the registered office, the number of directors and supervisors, officer appointment methods, and provisions allowing board action by written consent to permit remote governance.
required_dossiers: MOEA Investment Commission approval letter
Bank share capital remittance receipt/inward remittance certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Shareholder's written consent/resolution to incorporate and subscribe
Notarization or legalization certificate for foreign corporate resolutions
Directors' and supervisor's consent to act forms
Registered office address proof (lease or certificate of ownership)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the remittance, submit the Investment Commission approval and a remittance purpose declaration; if the notary questions foreign corporate authority, obtain a fresh apostilled or legalized board resolution and file it as an attachment. Correct any inconsistency between the remittance amount and the registered capital before notarization to avoid re-registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Registration and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commerce — One-Stop Company and Business Registration Online Gateway.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official Application for Company Registration on the MOEA one-stop portal by entering the approved company name, registered office address, capital, share structure, directors and supervisor, and business scope. Upload the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the investment approval letter, the share capital remittance receipt, paid-in capital statement confirmed by an independent certified public accountant, consent-to-act declarations for each statutory officer, and the registered office lease with landlord's usage consent matching an information service use. Pay the prescribed registration fee using the portal's e-payment function. The Department of Commerce then verifies whether the articles and application meet the Companies Act requirements and whether the business scope is legal and consistent with content classification. When approved, the authority issues the Certificate of Incorporation and, after tax registration, the Business Registration Certificate with the Uniform Invoice number.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application (form generated by one-stop portal)
Approved Articles of Incorporation with notarization stamp
Foreign Investment approval letter
Paid-in capital statement certified by a Taiwan CPA
Inward remittance certificate
Consent-to-act forms of all statutory officers
Registered office lease with building usage consent
Proof of company name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for missing attachments, upload the specific supplementary documents within the 15-day curative period. If registration is rejected for an illegal business scope, amend the Articles of Incorporation to narrow the scope and execute a new shareholder resolution; if the rejection is based on incomplete capital evidence, obtain a corrected bank certificate and, if necessary, re-notarize the Statement of Paid-in Capital and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, and Operational Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of Taipei (or local district tax office), Taipei City Government Department of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance and Bureau of Health Insurance; Financial Supervisory Commission-regulated banks.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, register the company with the tax authority for corporate income tax, business tax, and uniform invoicing, and obtain the taxpayer identification number. If hiring staff, register with the labor insurance bureau, national health insurance administration, and pension fund system; file the employees' work rules and any mandatory policies. Activate the operational bank account by presenting the board resolution, incorporation certificate, seal registration certificate, and passport/ID of board appointees, and sign the bank signature cards. Connect the merchant settlement accounts authorized in the board resolution with Apple App Store In-App Purchase and Google Play Billing by executing app store agreements and listing the Taiwan bank account as the payout destination. Ensure the tax registration is integrated with the company registration so that the Business Registration Certificate reflects the same office address.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate (post-registration tax certificate)
Company seal and responsible person seal registration certificate
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and payment rail settlement
Tax form for establishing taxpayer entity (BossNet or local collection form)
Passport or National Identification Card of responsible person
Bank account application and specimen signature cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed by mismatched address or seal, notify the MOEA one-stop desk and reprint the business certificate; if bank account activation is refused, request a written refusal reason and amend the signature authorization with a board supplemental resolution or provide additional ownership identity certificates from the foreign shareholder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Digital Content Compliance and Post-Registration Certification (No Physical License Required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Digital Affairs (moda) and National Communications Commission (NCC), Taiwan; local fire and environmental departments act only if physical premises are altered.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because the business scope under ISIC 9000 and NAICS 511130 is a pure digital platform for web fiction serialization and application-based reading, no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing license, no civil defense fire permit, and no environmental impact assessment are required. The company should nevertheless complete any voluntary digital content registrations, age-rating declarations for serialized fiction, personal data protection registration, and cybersecurity process by submitting to the mandatory digital economy platform rules of the Ministry of Digital Affairs if the platform stores user data in Taiwan. The company must maintain a permanent file denominated 'Physical Licensing Exemption Record' containing this assessment and the EIA exemption certificate from the Environmental Protection Administration, plus confirm that all payments via Apple IAP and Google Play Billing are reported to the tax authority. If later the company adds a warehouse or physical office with high occupancy, the local fire department should be asked to inspect emergency exits and fire extinguishers, and a fixed amount of fire insurance may be required by the landlord or bank, but no separate industrial license will be triggered.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate with ISIC/NAICS-aligned scope
EIA exemption/self-assessment statement
Personal Data Protection Act filing (if applicable)
Age-rating and content policy declarations for web novel platform
Apple Developer Program Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement
Tax receipt and uniform invoice registration
Existing physical licensing exemption record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NCC or moda notifies a content registration deficiency, correct the digital content classification and file a response within ten days; if an unpaid tax invoice or payment channel issue is flagged by the tax authority, issue a correction invoice and pay the assessed business tax with interest. If a landlord or branch operation requires a local fire inspection because office capacity is increased, schedule a fire safety inspection and obtain a certificate of compliance for record-only civil defense clearance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable — ISIC 9000 digital web fiction platform; no physical industrial project is executed.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable — no statutory operating license is required for pure internet content publishing; only Business Registration Certificate and digital content registrations apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan (ROC) — Not Applicable
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable — no construction, manufacturing, or discharge facilities; EIA not required under Article 4 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable — zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation; no compliance thresholds are applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable — no factory, warehouse, chemical plant, or assembly line to certify. Civil Defense fire permit and industrial occupational safety license are not required for an office-only digital content company; if a physical office is occupied, a general fire safety check under Taiwan Fire Services Act may be needed and a simple workplace safety policy under the Occupational Safety and Health Act remains advisory.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: China WFOE: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, Electronic Tax Office at etax.chinatax.gov.cn; Taiwan nexus: Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan, electronic tax filing portal at etax.nat.gov.tw and e-Invoice platform at einvoice.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: China: after formation under the Foreign Investment Law, the WFOE obtains a Unified Social Credit Code from the State Administration for Market Regulation; this code is the statutory Tax Identification Number. Tax registration must be completed within 30 days through the Electronic Tax Office, where the WFOE files entity particulars, selects VAT taxpayer status, registers for corporate income tax and payroll codes, and applies for fully digitalized electronic invoice issuance. Taiwan: because the WFOE supplies electronically delivered subscription services to Taiwan private consumers, it is a foreign electronic service provider under the Business Tax Act. If annual Taiwan-source turnover exceeds NT$480,000, it must appoint a Taiwan tax agent and file simplified tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau through the MOF e-Tax portal, attaching the Chinese incorporation certificate, Unified Social Credit Code, tax agent appointment letter, and a declaration that it has no fixed place of business in Taiwan; the Bureau then issues a dedicated Taiwan Business Tax Identification Number for the foreign e-commerce operator.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election is available under either China or Taiwan law. China

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), with supplementary oversight from the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (CBIRC) for banking institution licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese RMB (CNY) is fully convertible on the current account for legitimate trade and service transactions, including cross-border licensing fees and royalty payments; however, the capital account remains strictly controlled with mandatory registration, verification, and post-monitoring by SAFE. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) in mainland China, inbound foreign direct investment (FDI) must be routed through a designated SAFE-registered capital account, and every injection must be tied to the enterprise's registered business scope. Current-account settlements, on the other hand, are permissible through a properly documented corporate foreign exchange account, yet banks are required to verify the authenticity and legality of the underlying transaction before processing. Profit remittance to an overseas shareholder is permitted but requires annual audited financial statements, full tax clearance certificates, and a board resolution, all of which are assessed by the bank against the entity's dated profitability and cash-flow position. Export proceeds from digital content services, such as webnovel royalties, are not subject to a forced surrender ratio under the current SAFE framework; the WFOE may retain foreign exchange in a current-account FX settlement account or voluntarily convert to RMB at the bank's actual quotation. The principal hurdle in capital account convertibility lies in the requirement for ground-truth proof of the FDI capital's source and legitimate use, while profit outbound remittances are further constrained by the need for tax withholding on distributed dividends and the submission of evidence that the accumulated profits exceed any historical losses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory statutory conversion ratio for export foreign exchange receipts under the current SAFE regulatory regime. However, all export proceeds, including income from cross-border digital content licensing, must be repatriated to a designated mainland China bank account within 30 days after the contractual payment due date or, in the absence of a clear due date, within 90 days from the date of the underlying invoice or service completion certificate. Once credited, the WFOE may elect to hold the funds in its foreign exchange settlement account or convert them into RMB at any time, subject to filing through the bank's online current-account transaction management system and the presentation of the relevant trade-in-services contracts, invoices, and e-commerce transaction logs.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Revolut, Airwallex, or Payoneer that do not hold a duly granted banking license from the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission cannot legally provide primary corporate bank accounts or domestic CNY clearing rails for a mainland-incorporated WFOE. Such offshore EMIs are stripped of any local account-forming capacity because they lack the statutory ability to open settlement accounts in RMB, access the China National Clearing Center, or host mandated compliance interviews with statutory directors. Consequently, the viability of deploying an offshore EMI as the primary treasury rail is extremely low, and any attempt to use one for capital injection, profit repatriation, or invoice settlement would be rejected by Chinese banks at the point of fund entrance, while capital controls require all foreign exchange to pass through licensed bank channels. An EMI might serve solely as a secondary collection vehicle for overseas retail platform payments, but monies must still be aggregated and repatriated through a licensed Tier-1 bank to maintain lawful compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For all tier-1 corporate bank onbaording in mainland China, the statutory legal representative of the WFOE must appear physically at a designated branch in order to complete the corporate account activation interview and execute the Customer Due Diligence (CDD) package. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognised as an acceptable substitute under the People's Bank of China Account Settlement Measures and the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law. In exceptional scenarios, banks may permit a power of attorney for supplementary administrative tasks, but the ultimate KYC interview with the statutory representative must be performed in-person in a bank conference room, with the identity card or valid passport, company seal, and original incorporation documents available for inspection and photocopying.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain of the Taiwanese parent entity preventing clear identification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised certificate of incumbency and full share register from the Taiwanese corporate registry; an organisational chart listing all natural persons holding more than 25% of the parent; audited financial statements of the parent for the last two fiscal years; and a bank-signed confirmation of the parent company's account relationship history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital injection showing a mismatch between the declared industry and the funding amount, raising suspicion of money laundering through trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed FDI investment agreement; SAFE FDI registration certificate; commercial invoice or remittance instruction showing the exact purpose code and contract reference; a legal opinion by a PRC law firm confirming that the webnovel platform operation is within the registered business scope; and a certified copy of the parent's board resolution authorising the capital remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital intellectual property and royalty payment exposure due to the absence of material evidence to substantiate the IP ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Both domestic and cross-border copyright registration certificates for the webnovel catalogue; an editorial and content-moderation compliance policy; a verified statement of transactional volume on Apple App Store and Google Play; and a PRC-licensed intermediary valuation report for the copyright asset's fair market value.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of the Taiwanese investor, triggering heightened due diligence both in Taiwan and mainland China.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration form signed by the investor; a Chinese tax and criminal record certificate for all natural-person shareholders; a detailed source-of-wealth questionnaire supported by bank statements and income tax returns of the investing entity; and an independent third-party due diligence report from a provider such as Refinitiv or Thomson Reuters showing no adverse sanctions hits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first obtain a unique FDI registration code from its local SAFE branch. The Taiwanese shareholder then initiates an international wire transfer from a Taiwanese bank using the Specific Investment Purpose Code 722010 (Investor Injection) into the WFOE's designated FDI capital account at the chosen tier-1 bank. After the bank receives the funds, a Chinese certified public accountant performs a capital verification and issues a formal Capital Contribution Verification Report, which enables the release of the funds for normal operational use. The foreign currency injection may be settled into RMB via the bank's capital-account settlement function at the official spot exchange rate, with the WFOE also required to submit a quarterly return on the actual usage of the injected capital through the SAFE post-monitoring system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Cross-border royalty payments to overseas content licensors and service providers will primarily be executed through the SWIFT MT103 corporate clearing rail under the current-account service trade category, using the standard purpose code 129 (Licenses and Royalties). For larger multi-thousand-dollar settlements, the bank will require a copy of the underlying license agreement, a pro-forma invoice, and the verified tax withholding certificate to prove that the PRC withholding tax has been computed and reserved. Conventional commercial letters of credit or documentary collections are not typical for digital webnovel services; they would only be applicable if the WFOE later exports physical books or branded merchandise, in which case a confirmed irrevocable sight L/C or a documentary collection through the bank's trade desk would be appropriate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB FX forwards with a maturity of up to 1 year backed by consented current-account exposure, requiring the bank to verify the real trade background.
Cross-currency swaps approved by SAFE for eligible capital-account hedging purposes, such as swapping the USD debt or investment exposure into RMB with a maximum tenor of 3 years.
FX options on a currency pair such as USD/CNY or TWD/CNY, provided the notional is fully hedged by the entity's accepted risk portfolio and the bank's internal credit lines.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are strictly prohibited for a mainland WFOE; offshore NDFs cannot be used as a legal hedge due to China's FX regulatory exclusivity, and any attempt to structure them through a Taiwan or Singapore vehicle would violate SAFE rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting resolution, business report and approved financial statements (filed under Taiwan Companies Act Art. 170/230)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Department of Commercial Affairs (MOEA Company Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held by 30 June; approved documents must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after the meeting, i.e. no later than 15 July for a calendar-year enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA issues correction order after expiry; non-compliance triggers NT$10,000–NT$50,000 fine and can cause repeated daily penalties; persistent default may lead to MOEA-initiated dissolution or deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual foreign-invested enterprise operation report, capital/ownership update and UBO confirmation (foreign-investment annual report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Investment Commission (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end (within six months after fiscal year-end); calendar-year deadline: 30 June annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory correction order followed by administrative fines of NT$24,000–NT$120,000; repeated non-compliance may cancel foreign-investment approval and require compulsory disposal of foreign-held shares.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax final return (營利事業所得稅結算申報)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May of the following tax year for calendar-year filers; extended deadline available only after formal approval of a non-calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers surcharge of 1% every two days overdue up to 15%, plus interest on unpaid tax; assessed deficiency attracts negligence penalty of up to 20% of unpaid tax and potential asset liens.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding income tax return (salaries, royalties, dividends, and payments to foreign licensors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January of the calendar year following the tax year for prior-year withholdings; separate quarterly remittances apply, but annual reporting is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-remitting withholding tax incurs fines of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 plus an additional 5% of underpaid withholding tax; negligence penalty up to 15% may also apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan Companies Act Art. 20, annual financial statements must be audited and certified by a licensed CPA when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million, when the competent authority requires an independent audit, or when the company is publicly traded or in an FSC-supervised industry. A private WFOE below these thresholds may prepare financial statements confirmed by shareholders/supervisors without CPA certification.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply Taiwan-IFRS (TIFRS). Non-public foreign-invested enterprises generally apply the Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS, Taiwan SME GAAP) unless voluntarily adopting TIFRS or required by MOEAIC/bank covenants; all books must be kept in New Taiwan Dollars (TWD) and Chinese-language accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not require a standalone annual UBO return; annual confirmation is embedded in the AGM-approved shareholder register review and the MOEAIC annual operation report. Any share transfer involving a foreign investor must receive prior MOEAIC approval and be recorded in the Register of Members before the next annual confirmation. The company must maintain a beneficial-owner ledger identifying the ultimate natural-person shareholder with 10% or greater interest (or controlling influence) and produce it to MOEA/NTA upon request.
